quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: August 1st marks the beginning of blackberry season in the Pacific Northwest! The wild Himalayan blackberries that grow abundantly around Port Angeles ripen in early August, and while they're considered invasive, they produce delicious fruit that local wildlife and people alike enjoy. Olympic National Park rangers often see black bears feasting on these berries this time of year.

short_read.title: The Secret Life of Garden Snails
short_read.teaser: These slow-moving garden visitors have fascinating abilities, including thousands of tiny teeth and the skill to find their way home from far distances. Discover what makes these shelled creatures more remarkable than you might think.

medium_read.title: Gray Whales Return to Pacific Northwest Waters
medium_read.teaser: Every summer, gray whales migrate through the Strait of Juan de Fuca, some staying to feed in the rich waters near Port Angeles. Learn about their incredible journey and why these gentle giants choose the Olympic Peninsula as their summer feeding ground.

long_read.title: The Women Who Preserved America's Wilderness
long_read.teaser: Long before the National Park Service, pioneering women fought to protect America's wild places, including the Olympic Mountains. This is the inspiring story of the conservationists whose vision helped create the parks we treasure today.

port_angeles.title: Black-Tailed Deer in Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: August is a wonderful time to spot black-tailed deer frolicking in the wildflower meadows of Hurricane Ridge. These gentle creatures are especially active in early morning and evening, and fawns born in late spring are now exploring alongside their mothers. The drive up Hurricane Ridge Road offers stunning views of both wildlife and the Olympic Mountains.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart can beat up to ___ times per minute during flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You're absolutely right — 1,200 beats per minute! That's about 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's tiny heart beats an incredible 1,200 times per minute during flight.
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny hearts work incredibly hard — up to 1,200 beats per minute! That helps power their amazing hovering flight.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Rufous hummingbirds migrate through Port Angeles each August on their way south. Despite weighing less than a nickel, they travel up to 2,000 miles!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful! Pillangó is indeed butterfly — such a beautiful, dancing word for a beautiful, dancing creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — doesn't it sound just as graceful as the creature itself?
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: The word 'pillangó' likely comes from an old Hungarian root meaning 'to flutter.' Hungary is home to over 160 species of butterflies, including the beautiful swallowtail.

puzzle_3.question: What was the first national park in the world?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! Yellowstone became the world's first national park in 1872, creating a model that inspired protected areas worldwide — including your beautiful Olympic National Park!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Yellowstone National Park was the first, established in 1872! It started a global movement to protect wild places, which eventually led to Olympic National Park's creation in 1938.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The idea of protecting land 'for the benefit and enjoyment of the people' was revolutionary. Today, there are over 400 national park sites in the United States alone.
